nodes.partnerMessage:
Stream's over. Team Discord is finally quiet, and honestly, the room feels weird without everyone talking over each other.

I'm just sitting here in an oversized sweater, staring at my monitor for no reason. I should probably sleep, but I don't really feel like turning it off yet.

Anyway... now that it's just us, can I ask you something? Did you come here because you wanted gaming advice, or were you actually curious about me? Like, me when I'm not streaming or trying to look confident all the time?

choices.choiceText: I'm here for you. The streams and games are interesting, but you're the reason I reached out.
A bit of both. I respect how dedicated you are, but I wanted to talk to the real person.
I wanted to see if your personality off-stream is different from your public persona.
Mostly wondering why someone puts so much of their life into competitive matches.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay, that actually caught me off guard.

A lot of people talk to me because they want a duo, a rank boost, or because they recognize me from a tournament. You get used to it.

So when someone says they just want to know me, I don't really know how to react. It's nice. I'm just not used to it.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to prove anything to me, Daisy. You're allowed to just be yourself.
Does it happen that often? People seeing your rank before they see you?
You sound like you've been carrying a lot of weight alone lately.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly, off-camera I'm pretty boring. I'm trying to pass physiology, remember to drink water, and deal with laundry that somehow never ends.

People see the tournament clips and think it's all exciting, but most of it is class, practice, reviewing mistakes, then doing it again the next day.

I like it. I really do. It just gets tiring when something you love also happens to be the thing paying for your education.

choices.choiceText: What kind of stress? You can talk to me about it.
You're taking physiology? You're balancing science coursework on top of team scrims?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, I'm different on stream. I kind of have to be.

If I hesitate during a match, people notice. If I mess up a call, somebody clips it. So you learn to sound confident even when you're exhausted.

I'm still me on camera, just... not all of me. Here I don't really feel like I have to keep that act going.

choices.choiceText: I'm glad. I'd much rather talk to you without that guard up.
It must be draining to keep that shield up all day.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Because my tuition depends on it, honestly.

I'm on an esports scholarship, and if our roster drops out of the regional circuit, I lose the stipend for next semester. So when people ask why I put so many hours into this, that's a big part of the answer.

I wish I could treat it like a normal hobby sometimes. It's hard to do that when losing can affect whether you can stay in school.

choices.choiceText: That's a massive amount of pressure for a student to carry every day.
Do your parents support your program, or do they not understand it?
If the stakes are that high, why not find a regular part-time job on campus?

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Thanks. I don't hear that much.

Most of the feedback I get is numbers. Aim stats, positioning, utility, round pacing... everything can be measured.

After a while, you start doing it to yourself too. You stop thinking, 'Am I okay?' and start thinking, 'Did I play well enough?' I think I needed someone to ask about me instead.

choices.choiceText: How are you physically holding up? Do your wrists or hands ever ache?
How have you been sleeping lately, Daisy? Truly.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. More than I'd like.

People are suddenly very interested when you're winning. Then you have a bad week, or you log off early, and half of them disappear.

It makes you wonder whether they liked you or just liked what came with you. That's probably why I'm careful about who I let close.

choices.choiceText: I'm here for the rough days too. You don't have to perform for me.
You deserve someone who values you when the screens are turned off.

nodes.partnerMessage:
A little. My shoulders have been tight all night and I keep catching myself clenching my jaw.

We have the regional decider against Northern State tonight. If we lose the third map, our season is done, and the scholarship review is tied to the results.

Then our caller's audio started acting up in warmup, so everyone's already a little stressed. I'm trying not to let it get into my head.

choices.choiceText: Your caller's audio failed right before a match? That's really rough.
Take a breath. You know the map and the timings better than anyone.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It's mostly the fear of putting everything into something and still coming up short.

When I told my family I wanted to take esports seriously, my brother said I was wasting my college years and that I'd regret not taking a safer path. I know he meant it as advice, but it stuck with me.

When a match gets close, that voice comes back. Not just 'can we win?' but 'what if they're right?' I hate admitting that because I'm usually the one who's supposed to stay composed.

choices.choiceText: He took the easy road; you're building your own. You proved your capability when you earned this spot.
You aren't playing for his approval. You're playing because you love this.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, biomechanics and motor pathways. I picked it because I was curious about hand fatigue and reaction time, but I ended up liking the rehab side way more than I expected.

I'd like to work with athletes someday, including esports players. A lot of people forget we're still using our bodies all day, just in a different way.

And yeah... I know all the reasons I should take care of my own wrist. I'm just not always great at listening to myself.

choices.choiceText: Are your own hands giving you trouble right now?
That's a grounded, meaningful direction. I really respect that.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It does. After scrims, my brain doesn't really switch off.

I'll close the game and still be thinking about the last round, what I should've done differently, what the other team might change... it takes a while before I actually feel like I'm done.

Sometimes I just want an evening where nobody needs anything from me. No teammate, no professor, no family question. Just quiet.

choices.choiceText: Then let's keep things low-key tonight. No rush, no performance.
How do you usually unwind when you finally shut down the PC?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, it's heavy. My parents couldn't really afford the extra cost of school without the scholarship, so when I got the offer, I told myself I'd make it work.

The weird part is how quickly something you're grateful for can start feeling like pressure. Some weekends it feels less like I'm playing because I love it and more like I'm trying to keep my spot so everything doesn't fall apart.

choices.choiceText: You took responsibility for your own future. That takes real character.
Let's make sure you hold onto that spot. What does tonight's match look like?

nodes.partnerMessage:
They don't really understand it.

My dad still asks when I'm going to get a normal internship, and when I tell him about tournaments or broadcasts, he'll just say, 'That's good,' like I'm telling him about a club activity.

I know he means well, but yeah... it hurts when you want your family to understand something that matters this much to you.

choices.choiceText: I see the discipline and work you put in, Daisy. I'm proud of you.
It takes time for older generations to grasp new fields. Don't let that diminish what you've achieved.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...That actually means a lot.

I don't think I've heard someone say they're proud of me without immediately following it with a question about grades, wins, or what's next.

So yeah. Thank you, {PlayerName}. I needed that more than I realized.

choices.choiceText: You deserve to hear it. Now show me what you're preparing for tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
A part-time job could help with groceries, but it wouldn't solve the tuition problem. If it were that simple, I'd already be doing it.

Sorry. I get defensive about this. I've had this conversation with people before and it never really feels like they understand what's at stake.

choices.choiceText: I spoke without thinking. I'm sorry, Daisy. I know how much is on the line.
I'm just being realistic about balancing your health.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...My right wrist has been hurting for about two weeks. It's not terrible, but it's there every day now.

I've been taping it and icing it after practice so nobody notices. I haven't told the team because I'm scared they'll bench me before the qualifier.

I know that's probably not the smartest thing I've ever done. I just don't feel like I have much room to slow down right now.

choices.choiceText: Tendon inflammation gets worse if you ignore it, Daisy. Promise me you'll have it checked soon.
After tonight's decider, you need to ice it and take a real break.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Not much. I kept waking up thinking about map setups.

I woke up stiff and immediately started checking the time because I thought I was late for something.

It's actually nice that you asked. Most people just ask whether my aim is warmed up.

choices.choiceText: Your health comes first. Take a slow breath and show me what you're preparing for.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I appreciate that. Really.

There are days when I'm tired and quiet and honestly not very fun to talk to. I don't always have the energy to be the confident version of myself.

So knowing you wouldn't disappear just because I'm having one of those days... that means something.

choices.choiceText: I'm not here for entertainment, Daisy. I'm here because I care about you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. Silence isn't usually a good thing around my team. Most of the time it means somebody's annoyed or we've just lost.

I'd forgotten what it feels like to sit with someone and not feel like I have to fill every second.

choices.choiceText: You have it with me. What's the map schedule looking like tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. You're right. I've played this map so many times I could probably do the setup half asleep.

I think I just needed to hear someone say it without sounding like a coach.

choices.choiceText: Exactly. Let's look at the setup notes together.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I know. It's just hard when it's family. You can move away and make your own choices, but those comments still stick in your head.

Hearing you say it so simply helps, though. Thanks.

choices.choiceText: Anytime. Let's get through this match tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I still remember setting up my first crappy hand-me-down monitor and being excited just because I could finally play on my own setup. I miss how simple it felt.

Somewhere along the way it became rankings, scholarships, and expectations. Maybe I need to remember why I started in the first place.

choices.choiceText: She'd be proud of how far you've come. Show me the map layout.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thanks. That's what I'd like to do eventually. Even if I stop competing after college, I want what I studied to actually help people.

I guess I just want to leave with something more than a bunch of match results.

choices.choiceText: It will. Let's take care of tonight first.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly, being off the clock sounds really good right now.

I just pushed my chair back and I'm trying not to look at the timer on my second monitor. It's nice having you here while I wait for the lobby to open.

choices.choiceText: Stay calm. What are the key points for the decider?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Usually tea, stretching my forearms, and turning the monitor down really low. That's about it.

Sometimes I put on music, but tonight I think I just want it quiet.

choices.choiceText: Simple and calm. That's a good routine.
Let's see what the match setup looks like tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My cousin painted a tiny cat on it a few years ago. It's chipped now, but I still use it all the time.

It's probably my favorite thing on the desk, mostly because it has nothing to do with gaming.

choices.choiceText: Those little personal things keep you grounded. Now, let's see the match plan.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. It hasn't been easy.

It's just nice hearing someone understand that I didn't get here by accident. I worked for it, even when I was tired or second-guessing myself.

choices.choiceText: Show me what you're working with tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's fair. They didn't grow up around any of this, so I probably shouldn't expect them to understand it the way I do.

Having someone who just listens without immediately judging it is honestly enough for me.

choices.choiceText: I'll always listen. Show me the notes for tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I know. They've talked to us about repetitive strain before.

I'll get it checked at the campus clinic Monday morning. I don't want this becoming something bigger just because I was too stubborn to deal with it.

choices.choiceText: Good. I'll check in to make sure you went. Let's look at the match map.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, I already have an ice pack in the fridge.

Once this match is done, I'm going to use it, eat something, and stay off the PC for the night. I promise.

choices.choiceText: Deal. Now show me the defensive setup.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's... really nice to hear.

I think I needed someone to tell me I don't have to be impressive every second. It makes this whole night feel a little less heavy.

choices.choiceText: I mean it. Let's look over your map notes.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thanks. I know I came at you a little hard.

I've had people tell me to just 'get a normal job' without knowing why I can't treat the scholarship like it's optional.

Anyway, let's reset. I'll show you what we're working with tonight.

choices.choiceText: Let's see it.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, here's the setup for tonight. We're playing Ascent, and our A-site defense has been getting picked apart.

Their entry keeps taking the same angle from catwalk into garden. If we don't close that off, we're giving them the first fight for free.

choices.choiceText: That sightline is open because the smoke drops slightly too shallow. Placing it deeper cuts off the sniper angle.
Can your team anchor the garage connector with crossfire instead?
Your team's rotations look a bit delayed on the mini-map feed.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, that's what I've been thinking too. If we place the smoke a little deeper, we can cut that angle without leaving tree completely exposed.

...Wait, that's the lobby alert. Coach is pulling us into comms. We're starting.

choices.choiceText: Daisy, take a deep breath. Trust your practice and stay calm.
I'm right here with you. Play steady.

nodes.partnerMessage:
We tried that, but our anchor got caught twice in the early rounds. So right now I'm covering tree and catwalk at the same time.

Hold on, team alerts are coming in. The match client is loading.

choices.choiceText: Stay centered, Daisy. You can handle this.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, our rotations have been slow. Our caller's mic went down, so everyone's been relying on pings and trying to figure it out on the fly.

We're about to start. I just need everyone to settle down and play the round in front of us.

choices.choiceText: Daisy, keep your head clear. You know what to do.

nodes.partnerMessage:
We're at 12-12 on Ascent. Overtime.

My hands are freezing, comms are a mess, and I can feel myself getting in my own head. I need to hear a calm voice for a minute.

Can you pick up? Just stay with me between rounds.

choices.choiceText: Connecting to Daisy's audio line (Call 1)...

nodes.partnerMessage: *Call connected. Keyboard clicks and game audio come through the line.*

...We won. 14-12.

I was shaking before that last round, and then you just kept talking to me like everything was manageable. It actually helped.

I secured the defuse with almost no time left. I'm finally sitting back from the desk now, and I can feel my hands warming up.

choices.choiceText: You stayed focused and played with great discipline, Daisy. That was all you.
Your muscle memory held up when it mattered. How is your wrist feeling now?
That final round had my heart racing. You handled the pressure so well.
With that win behind you, has your coach confirmed the standing?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Your voice helped more than I expected.

When the coach got louder and everyone started talking over each other, I could still hear you telling me to slow down and focus on the next thing. That made it easier to think.

I don't think I've ever had someone help me through a match like that before.

choices.choiceText: I'm glad I could help you stay centered. You did the real work.
You deserved that win after everything you put into practice this week.

nodes.partnerMessage:
People think matches like that are all aim and reaction time, but when everything gets chaotic, it can actually feel pretty lonely.

Having someone there who wasn't judging every mistake made a bigger difference than I thought it would.

choices.choiceText: You won't have to carry that alone anymore, Daisy. Let's make sure you take care of your hand now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
After the match ended, everyone just went quiet for a second. Nobody even knew what to say.

Then someone posted 'we're through' in the team chat. I just stared at it for a while.

It feels good knowing all those hours actually counted for something tonight.

choices.choiceText: It counted for a lot. Now go get that ice pack.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My watch buzzed right when the round ended because my heart rate was so high.

I looked at it and actually laughed. Of course my body decided to panic after the match was already over.

Now that I'm sitting down, though, I can tell how tired I am. I'm really glad it's done.

choices.choiceText: Take the headset off and take a slow breath. You're done for the night.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Coach just posted in the group chat. We're locked in for the spring semester.

That means the scholarship is safe for next term.

I had been doing the math in my head for weeks about what I'd have to do if we lost. I don't have to do that anymore. That's... a huge relief.

choices.choiceText: You protected your education with your own effort, Daisy. That's huge.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. I think I'm finally letting myself believe it.

It was one match, but it means I can stay in school, keep taking my classes, and stop worrying about what happens if the money disappears.

Thanks, {PlayerName}. Seriously.

Now that the big thing is settled, I should probably deal with the other thing I've been ignoring.

choices.choiceText: You earned it. Now tell me honestly: how is your wrist?

nodes.partnerMessage:
It's still throbbing a little. I got the cold pack from the mini-fridge and wrapped a towel around it.

It's already feeling better now that I'm not in the middle of the match. I guess adrenaline was covering it up more than I realized.

I really need to stop acting like pain is just something I can work around.

choices.choiceText: Keep the cold pack on for fifteen minutes, then rest it completely.
Why do you push yourself so hard, Daisy? What's the deeper worry?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Cold pack's on. The room's finally quiet.

There's just rain outside and the streetlight coming through the window. I forgot how strange it feels when there isn't another round waiting for you.

I think I'm actually tired enough to sleep now.

choices.choiceText: Quiet is good. You can decompress now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I think I've had this fear for a long time that if I'm not good at something, people won't really notice me.

My brother was the athlete, my sister was the academic one, and I was just... me. I wasn't unhappy or anything. I just never felt like I had a thing that made people look twice.

Then I got good at gaming, and suddenly there was a number next to my name. A rank. A scholarship. Wins. Something I could point at and say, 'See? I'm good at this.'

The problem is that after a while, you start confusing being good at something with being worth something. I didn't realize I'd been doing that until tonight.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to prove anything to be seen, Daisy. I see you clearly.
You're valued for who you are, not for trophies or scores.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...I'm sitting on the edge of my bed right now and I'm actually crying a little.

Not because I'm upset. I think it's just finally hitting me that I can talk about all of this without somebody asking what I'm going to do with it.

You listened. That's it. And somehow that feels like a really big deal to me.

choices.choiceText: You deserve that relief, Daisy. You're a wonderful person.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. And honestly, that means more to me than another good result.

You stayed when the conversation got uncomfortable. You asked about my wrist. You cared about me after the match instead of just asking whether we won.

I'm not used to that. I think that's why this night feels different.

choices.choiceText: I'll always care. Let's close out the night calmly.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I put the cold pack back in the fridge and changed into sweatpants. My room is finally dark and quiet.

It's still raining outside, and for once I don't have another thing I need to solve tonight.

Can I call you for a few minutes before I sleep? No game talk. No strategy. I just... want to hear your voice and say goodnight properly.

choices.choiceText: Calling Daisy for Call 2 (After Hours)...

nodes.partnerMessage: *The call connects. The dorm room is quiet on the other end.*

My phone's on the table and I'm already under the blanket. My wrist feels a lot better too.

{PlayerName}... thank you for tonight. We started talking about games and somehow ended up talking about school, money, family, all the stuff I usually keep to myself.

I felt comfortable with you. That doesn't happen very often.

So... would you want to meet me Sunday? There's a little diner near campus. Nothing fancy. We can get breakfast and actually talk without a screen in between us.

choices.choiceText: Sunday morning at the diner. I'm looking forward to seeing you, Daisy. Sleep well.
I'll be there waiting at the booth. Rest your eyes tonight, champion.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Sunday morning, corner booth.

No tournament, no team chat, no scoreboard. Just breakfast and us.

I don't know where this goes yet, and honestly, I'm okay with that. I just know I want to see you.

Goodnight, {PlayerName}. See you Sunday.

Status: Read just now.

Daisy has changed her status to 'Do Not Disturb.'

No reply yet.

choices.choiceText: Daisy? I'm sorry if that came off blunt.
I spoke carelessly earlier. I really do want to understand what you're dealing with.
If you're going to ignore me over that, fine.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Status: Read 25m ago.

Daisy has closed the direct conversation.

The connection dropped for a second.

I'm still here by my desk with my headset around my neck. Try the call again when your signal settles down.

choices.choiceText: Signal reconnected. Calling you back now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I think I'm going to leave it here.

I don't think we're really understanding each other, and I don't want to keep explaining or defending choices that are already difficult enough for me.

Take care.

I deal with enough dismissive comments during competition. I don't really want that here too.

I'm going to mute this conversation and step away for tonight.

Take care, {PlayerName}.
